notes.title: Vectromirror (Sequel) - Release Date
notes.content:
Dear Test Subjects,

First and foremost, thank you for playing our game!

We’re happy to announce that the sequel, Vectromirror, will be out on May 27th.
It’s been a long journey, and having you all play Vectromirror 0 helped immensely on the next title of the series. 

Check out the Vectromirror Steam Page
(if you haven’t done it yet).  

Features
New Aesthetics
Each level has it’s own art, based on each of the (6) emotions that you’ll go through during the narrative.
Narrative
This sequel includes a much deeper narrative about AI and human emotions, telling the full story of the series, all through Voice Acting (includes English subtitles).
More gameplay
The game is longer, includes new mechanics, and also non-linear levels to explore.

Join our Discord server. If you are looking for a place to chat about the game and join other speedrunners, that’s the place! 

To remain up-to-date with news from Vectromirror, connect with us here:
Official Website
Facebook
Twitter
Instagram

Have fun!

The Vectromirror Initiative

notes.title: Patch Notes #8 - Jan 13th, 2022 [V0.1649]
notes.content:
Dear Test Subjects,

First and foremost, thank you for playing our game.

Version: 0.1649

What’s New
Epilepsy Warning
Due to the game having flashing lights, we decided to add this warning, so that those who suffer from epilepsy are informed about this aspect of the game. 
The warning appears as soon as you start the game.

Developer’s Notes
Future of Vectromirror 0
We’ve been working hard on the premium version and sequel,  Vectromirror, which is getting a big update soon.
Our team has been focusing on that version of the project, and therefore we haven’t made a lot of updates for this version.
That being said, we’d like to mention that we do have more plans for Vectromirror 0, which we can’t comment yet (but rest assured that more content is in our plans =D). 


Make sure to check it out!

notes.title: Patch Notes #7 - Jun 19th, 2021 [V0.1478]
notes.content:
Dear Test Subjects,

First and foremost, thank you for playing our game.

Version: 0.1478

What’s New
Coyote Jump
Delay for still being able to jump after leaving a platform (a.k.a. Coyote Jump) added.
This addition will help players not skip the first jump, which sometimes can bring the perception that the second jump is not working, where in fact the player had left the platform (late jump). 

Vectromirror Update
New levels, major bug fixes, subtitles and more
The premium version of Vectromirror, which is the sequel of this version, just received A HUGE UPDATE!
The new levels are doubling the duration of the experience, at no extra cost. =D
Added 2 new levels: Love and Rage, making the experience more wholesome. 
Added voice-over for all levels, including the new ones. 
Subtitles system added for the voiceovers
New mechanics added: Grapple Cube and Overclock
New area inside the level Trust
Voice over for the level Misery
Major bug fixes (over 150 squashed!)

Make sure to check it out!
LINK

Developers Note
We’ve been super busy with Vectromirror (premium version), and for that reason, we haven’t been doing many updates for Vectromirror 0. 
But rest assured that we have more plans for the free version as well, so keep tuned!

Please let us know your thoughts in our Discord server. If you are looking for a place to chat about the game and join other speed runs, that’s the place!

notes.title: Patch Notes #5 - Oct 5th, 2020
notes.content:
Dear Test Subjects,

First and foremost, thank you for playing our game.

Version: 0.890

What’s New
Speedrun Timer Options
Inside the Main Menu, under Options, players can enable the “Timer Options”, which allows players to have an in-game timer. 
The timer will be present throughout the levels, providing feedback in real-time. 
When enabled, the Main Menu will keep track of your Total Time, as well as per level. 
After your first run with the timer, it will keep track of your best run, as well as your last run, so players can have the feedback on which levels they need to improve. 
Only full playthroughs will update the Total Time.  

New Vectromirror™ Endgame Reward
Our full game, Vectromirror™ is releasing October 13th, 2020. We’ve added a special endgame reward to those able to beat Vectromirror 0™.
We’ve added something special to the endgame after the final level.


Visual Improvements
Level 2
In the last room of the level, the hazard area received some improvements.
Added frame around the entire area.
Minor improvements to materials and walls, to improve aesthetics.

notes.content:

Save System
Previously, when the player used a Level Select option to enter a level, sometimes the player would not enter the correct place inside of the level or game. 

Optimization
Removed motion blur, which will improve the experience for players by increasing the frame rate.
Optimized game files to decrease load and build size (was 4.4gb and now is 2.9gb)

Tutorial Messages
In-game readable texts were slightly increased, to improve readability. 

Bug Fixes

Player won’t lose any progress when updating the game.
Player Interaction with Physics Objects
Adjustments that were still needed have now been made, and overall stability is improved.

notes.title: Patch Notes #3 - Aug 16th, 2020
notes.content:
Dear Test Subjects,

First and foremost, thank you for playing our game.

Improvements

Player Interaction with Physics Objects
There was some instability when The Subject steps onto a Physics Object. 

Player can step onto Physics Objects with more stability.
Some adjustments are still being done to improve these interactions. 

Input Mapping Options
We received requests to allow the player more options for Control key assignment. 
In the Main Menu, go to Options, and then Input Mapping, to change the buttons/keys. 
 We are still improving this feature.  

Wallrun Video Tutorial (in-game)
Some versions of The Subject were having difficulty understanding how the Wallrun mechanic works. 
In the Tutorial level’s Wallrun section, there’s a video showing how to properly activate the Wallrun (as well as how ‘not to do it’)  

Adjustments
 Player has more air control.
 Speed was slightly increased  

Bug Fixes

Moving Platform
Fixed issue with a level 1 moving platform that behaved inconsistently.
Push/Pull Force
Fixed issue with activation sound and power level persisting after pausing while using the power and going back to the main menu, and even loading into a new level.
Decreased full charge time.
Shortened delay that charged the ability (now it sticks around).
Fixed invisible objects interacting with the power. 
Wallrun
Fixed issue with camera tilting when activating the ability.

notes.title: Patch Notes #1 - July 17th 2020
notes.content:
Dear Test Subjects,

First and foremost, thank you for playing our game.

This first update includes performance improvements (via graphics options), improved wall-running, and options for sprinting (either toggle or hold).

Version: 0.495

Wall Run Improvements
We heard your feedback and decided to improve this mechanic.
It is now easier to attach to the wall with increased stability.
Player can also move the camera freely during the wall run without unsnapping from most walls.
Other minor tweaks to improve the movement flow.

Graphics Options
Depending on your  PC’s specs, you may benefit from lowering the graphics quality, to get a smoother running experience.
Through the Main Menu, you are now able to change the Graphics quality in these options:
Epic (default)
High
Medium
Low

Sprint Options
We decided to add a new option (“Hold”), for those who are not big fans of the “Toggle.”
The options available are:
Toggle (turn on/off)
Hold (active only when pressed)
